idea: Body parts & opposites – UP and DOWN (SUNNY PARK, OUTDOOR outfit): a big shiny red balloon floats up into the picture right beside Baby Ava's face ('Wow! Look! A big red balloon!'); chorus 'Up and down! Up and down!'; 'Up, up, up! My balloon goes up!' (she lifts the string high, the balloon rises); 'Down, down, down! My ball rolls down!' (a yellow ball rolls down the red slide to her); copy-me 'Arms up high! Arms down low!' (she stretches up and bends down); she asks the viewer 'Where does my balloon go? Hmm?' (pause) – 'Up! Up, up, up! Yay!'; lesson 'Up is high, down is low!'. Loop: the hook framing with the balloon beside her face, now with the yellow ball by her knee, bye-bye wave.
lesson: Opposites UP and DOWN (up = high, down = low).
calendar: Friday slot 1 – Body parts & opposites (big/small done 13 Nov; today up/down). New Short: no long video with status 'uploaded' and an unused clip in the last 21 days (13 Nov shapes long video was delivered, not uploaded).
characters: BABY AVA: a cute chubby 1-year-old baby girl with short fluffy curly brown hair, one small curly ponytail on top with a sparkly pink star hair clip, big brown eyes, rosy cheeks. wearing pink overalls over a yellow t-shirt with a small flower and white sneakers with pink laces.
supporting: SUPPORTING OBJECTS: RED BALLOON = one big shiny round plain red balloon on a thin white string (no print, no writing). YELLOW BALL = one plain bright yellow soft rubber ball, the size of a melon, no print.

learning.goal: Understand and say the opposites UP and DOWN: a balloon goes up, a ball rolls down; arms up high, arms down low.
learning.shown_how: Shot 1 the red balloon floats up beside her face; shot 2 she lifts the string high and the balloon rises UP into the sky; shot 3 one yellow ball rolls DOWN the red slide to her; shot 4 she stretches both arms UP high and DOWN low with the balloon above and the ball at her feet; shot 5 loop with balloon + ball.

learning.fact_check: Balloon (filled, light) rises UP – correct; ball rolls DOWN the slide – correct; arms up/down movements match the words. One balloon, one ball in every frame (counted). No letters/numbers in frames.
learning.modeling: Positive throughout; balloon string held/near her, no safety issue.
learning.toddler_fit: Simple words, bright calm park, one baby, big face, gentle play.

title: Wow! A Big Red Balloon! 🎈 Up and Down with Baby Ava | Learn Opposites | Crayon Babies
description:
Wow! A big red balloon floats up right next to Baby Ava in Sunny Park! 🎈 Sing along with Baby Ava and learn the opposites UP and DOWN: the balloon goes up, the ball rolls down the slide.

🎬 What happens in this video:
😮 "Wow! Look! A big red balloon!"
🎈 Up, up, up! My balloon goes up!
⚽ Down, down, down! My ball rolls down!
🙌 Arms up high! Arms down low! – stretch with Ava!
🤔 "Where does my balloon go?" – can you answer?
👋 Up is high, down is low! Bye bye, friends!

📚 Kids learn: opposites • up • down • high • low • first words for toddlers

🎶 Voices only: children singing, humming and clapping with a soft hand drum – no other musical instruments.

A fun sing-along opposites song for toddlers and preschoolers, with Baby Ava in Sunny Park playing with a red balloon and a yellow ball on the slide, plus an arms-up, arms-down movement game kids can copy at home.
